question:
In triangle \(ABC\) shown in the adjoining figure, \(M\) is the midpoint of side \(BC,\) \(AB=12,\) and \(AC=16.\) Points \(E\) and \(F\) are taken on \(AC\) and \(AB,\) respectively, and lines \(EF\) and \(AM\) intersect at \(G.\) If \(AE=2AF,\) then \(\frac{EG}{GF}\) equals

[Figure 1](figures/1975_AMC_12_Q28_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The midpoint condition suggests using areas: triangles with equal bases on \(BC\) and a common altitude have equal areas. Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\).

Since \(BM=CM\), we have \([ABM]=[ACM]\) and \([GBM]=[GCM]\). Subtracting the second pair from the first gives
\[
[ABG]=[ACG].
\]
Let their common positive area be \(S\), and put \(AF=x>0\). Then \(AE=2x\). Comparing triangles whose bases lie on the same side of \(ABC\), with common vertex \(G\), gives
\[
[AFG]=\frac{x}{12}S,
\qquad
[AEG]=\frac{2x}{16}S.
\]
Finally, triangles \(AEG\) and \(AFG\) have bases \(EG\) and \(GF\) on the same line and share the altitude from \(A\). Thus their area ratio is the requested length ratio:
\[
\frac{EG}{GF}
=\frac{[AEG]}{[AFG]}
=\frac{2x/16}{x/12}
=\frac32.
\]
The positive factors \(x\) and \(S\) cancel, so the answer is \(\boxed{\frac32}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
We can transfer the midpoint condition to segments parallel to \(EF\), then compare those segments with \(GF\) and \(GE\).

Through \(B\) and \(C\), draw lines parallel to \(EF\), meeting line \(AM\) at \(P\) and \(Q\), respectively. Extend \(AM\) as needed. Because \(MB\) and \(MC\) lie on one line, \(MP\) and \(MQ\) lie on another, and \(BP\parallel CQ\), triangles \(MBP\) and \(MCQ\) are similar by their equal angles. Their corresponding sides \(MB\) and \(MC\) are equal, so
\[
BP=CQ.
\]
Also, \(FG\parallel BP\), with \(A,F,B\) collinear and \(A,G,P\) collinear. Hence triangles \(AFG\) and \(ABP\) are similar, giving
\[
\frac{GF}{BP}=\frac{AF}{AB}.
\]
Likewise, triangles \(AEG\) and \(ACQ\) are similar, so
\[
\frac{EG}{CQ}=\frac{AE}{AC}.
\]
All these segments have positive length in the given configuration. Dividing the two ratios and using \(BP=CQ\) and \(AE=2AF\), we obtain
\[
\frac{EG}{GF}
=\frac{AE/AC}{AF/AB}
=\frac{2AF/16}{AF/12}
=\frac32.
\]
Thus the answer is \(\boxed{\frac32}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Construct equal parallel segments
